docs.title: 1. Summary
docs.text:
A world declares its layer 0 with four kinds of atoms:

kind Python record question it answers example (integer world) object ObjectSpec what exists? int operation OperationSpec what can be done in one step? +, succ, is-zero combinator CombinatorSpec how are steps put together? sequence, branch, recursion observation ObservationSpec what can the learner see? inputs and result

Two more kinds are definable (section 19): law (LawSpec, sigil #: a statement that always holds, usable as one rewrite step) and bridge (BridgeSpec, sigil ~: a translation whose diagram commutes). Worlds may give laws at layer 0 as axioms. Templates (TemplateSpec) produce definitions of any kind from kind and value parameters.

A learner or a generator writes definitions of any of the six kinds. Every definition is one Definition record and goes through one pipeline (section 9): written -> checked -> callable -> verified -> promoted. A promoted definition is used as one step under a chosen boundary (section 10). The four invariants (section 11) are hard rules.

The current Opulse (operations only, fixed combinators substitution / branch / recursion, fixed value types) is the special case "dialect legacy-v1" (section 13). Published worlds and data read unchanged through that dialect, except the clock world (section 14).

docs.title: 2.1 Value
docs.text:
Value = Int | Text | Card
Int   = an integer of unbounded size (bool is NOT an Int)
Text  = a finite sequence of Unicode code points
Card  = Card(sort: SortRef, tag: str, fields: tuple[Value, ...])
  • sort names the object (section 4) the card belongs to, with its static parameters, for example bool, list[int], perm[4], fraction.
  • tag is one of the tags the sort declares. A record sort has one tag (by convention the sort name). bool is the sort with tags false and true and no fields.
  • fields is an ordered tuple. A tag declares either a fixed list of named fields or one variable-length field list items: T (used by sequences such as list[T]).
  • Values are finite trees. There are no cycles and no infinite values (section 16).

Two values are equal (kernel equality) when they have the same constructor, the same sort and tag, and equal fields in order. Kernel equality is structural on the canonical representation (section 4.3). A world operation eq is a separate thing and may differ (for example an IEEE eq(NaN, NaN) = false in a bit-level float world).

docs.title: 2.2 JSON encoding (schema opulse.value/2)
docs.text:
{"t": "int", "v": 5}
{"t": "str", "v": "abc"}
{"t": "<sort>", "tag": "<tag>", "f": [<value>, ...]}

The legacy encodings {"t": "int"|"bool"|"str"|"list[int]"|"perm"|"note"|"melody"|"grid"|"state"|..., "v": ...} remain valid input and output in dialect legacy-v1. They are decoded with a world-context codec (section 13.3): the codec, not the tag alone, decides the sort.

docs.title: 2.3 Host representations
docs.text: A world may store a given sort in a host representation (Python int, tuple, Permutation, the robot state object) for speed. The world then must declare a codec to_card / from_card that is total and bijective on valid values. The host representation must not change any result, failure, step count or trace.

docs.title: 2.4 Integers derived from zero and successor
docs.text: The world successor (and new teaching worlds) may declare nat = compose <zero | succ(nat)> as an object. 3 then has the derivation succ(succ(succ(zero))). This derivation is unfoldable and costs three succ steps. The kernel still carries integers as Int; the derivation is a teaching object, not the carrier.

docs.title: 3. Outcome
docs.text:
Every evaluation returns an Outcome:

Outcome = Ok(value: Value) | Bottom(reason: str) | Unknown(resource: str)
  • Bottom(reason) is a domain failure: division by zero, a blocked robot move, no matching case arm, a value outside valid. Reasons are short identifiers (div_zero, blocked, no_branch, invalid, measure, overflow, nan_condition).
  • Unknown(resource) means the evaluation ran out of a resource: fuel (layer-0 step budget), depth, nodes. Unknown is not a value.
  • Calls and constructors are strict: a Bottom argument makes the call Bottom with the same reason; an Unknown argument makes it Unknown. Arguments evaluate left to right and evaluation stops at the first argument that is not Ok (later arguments are not evaluated and charge nothing). Let is strict in the same way. Dialect legacy-v1 differs (section 13.2, rule 8).
  • Comparison of outcomes (outcome_equal): Ok(a) == Ok(b) iff a equals b; Bottom(r1) == Bottom(r2) is true regardless of reason (legacy rule: two NaN are equal); Unknown is never equal to anything, including another Unknown. A grader must never judge an Unknown result correct.
  • Containers must not hold Bottom. To keep a failure as data, a definition must use the explicit lift: lift[T] = bot(reason: str) | val(T), built by the non-strict operation catch. defined(x) (legacy) is the non-strict test Bottom -> false.
  • Legacy codec: the legacy NaN value and {"t": "nan", ...} decode to Bottom; Bottom encodes back to the legacy NaN in dialect legacy-v1.

docs.title: 4.1 Forms
docs.text:
An object is declared by one of two methods plus one switch:

  1. compose: a sort is a set of tags; each tag has fields. Special cases:
  2. record: one tag with named fields, pair = compose <pair(a: int, b: int)>;
  3. variant: several tags, option[T] = compose <none | some(value: T)>;
  4. sequence: one tag with variable items, list[T] may be either the native sequence compose <items(T*)> or the structural compose <nil | cons(head: T, tail: list[T])>;
  5. recursive and mutually recursive sorts: declared together as one group. Each group must be strictly positive (a sort appears in its own fields only as a field type, never as a function argument) and must have at least one base tag (a tag whose fields do not mention the group) so that finite values exist.
  6. refine: refine base where valid; canon.
  7. base: an existing sort.
  8. valid: base -> bool: which representations are values.
  9. canon: base -> base (optional): the canonical representative.
  10. valid and canon are nodes over the single variable x (the base representation); record fields are read with the base sort's accessors, for example record.den(x).
  11. Obligations (each recorded as evidence, section 8): canon is total on valid values; idempotent (canon(canon x) = canon x); keeps validity (valid x -> valid(canon x)); and every interface operation respects canon (canon x = canon y -> op(x) = op(y), per argument position).
  12. valid and canon must be written in the terminating sublanguage: no Blocks/Jump; Rec only with a measure (section 6.3). A definition whose valid or canon can return Unknown on its verified scope must not be stored.
  13. seal (switch, sealed: true): only the operations listed in interface may build or read the inside. Other definitions see only the sort name and the interface. Unfolding for audit may still show the inside.

A named constant is an ObjectSpec with form constant. It introduces no new sort. Its body is a closed term of an existing sort, for example three = succ(succ(succ(zero))). Unfolding replaces the name with the term; evaluation charges the steps of the term.

docs.title: 4.2 Static parameters
docs.text: A sort may take static parameters: type parameters (list[T]) and integer parameters (perm[n], uint[k]). They are fixed at instantiation. Sizes known only at run time go into valid (the robot map width is checked by valid, not by a type parameter). A world constant (for example the name list of the rel world) read by valid is part of the world hash; a new constant value means a new world version.

docs.title: 4.3 Entry: make and the enter rule of each edge
docs.text:
Every input edge inputs[i] and the output edge of an operation declares an entry rule:

rule meaning bottom a value outside valid gives Bottom(invalid) normalize apply canon of the sort (for example n mod 12) saturate(lo, hi) clamp into the range fold(name) a named legacy folding rule (section 13.2)

The default for a refine sort is normalize when it has canon, else bottom. The check and the canonicalisation happen at the semantic position of make (the edge) and are charged there in exact layer-0 steps (canon_cost: counted), or declared free for a given layer-0 sort (canon_cost: free, part of the world version). Moving from a refine sort to its base is implicit. Narrowing from the base to the refine sort is explicit (make), except the legacy-v1 int->note rule (section 13.2).

docs.title: 4.4 Record
docs.text:
kind: object
name: fraction
form: refine
base: {record: {num: int, den: int}}
valid: "den(x) != 0"              # a Node over the variable x (section 6)
canon: "reduce x by gcd; den > 0" # a Node over x
sealed: true
interface: [make_fraction, num, den, fraction_eq]
params: []
equality: canonical               # canonical | none
canon_cost: counted

docs.title: 5. Operations: OperationSpec
docs.text:
kind: operation
name: add
role: combine                     # transform | combine | decide | relate | act
inputs: [{sort: byte, enter: bottom}, {sort: byte, enter: bottom}]
output: {sort: byte, enter: normalize}
rule: "(a + b) mod 256"           # human-readable rule, required
errors: []                        # Bottom reasons this operation can return
impl: {host: "<module>:add", digest: "<sha256 of the source>"}  # or {table: ...} or {body: <Node>}
cost: 1                           # exact layer-0 steps of one call
strict: true
reads_params: []
  • role is a label only. relate operations return set[lift[T]] (several results); act operations take and return a state sort (they change state).
  • impl.host is allowed only at layer 0 (given atoms). The digest of the host source goes into the world lock; a change of the source changes the world version. Definitions written by a learner or a generator must not use host code.
  • Every given operation must state its rule, its errors and its cost.
  • A host implementation must be a deterministic function of its arguments without side effects (state changes are new state values returned, never mutation). Memoized recursion, fast paths and replay rely on it; an atom that mutates its arguments is outside the model. The cost of a call may be a declared function of the arguments (cost_rule), charged before the call.
  • Comparison operations of legacy worlds (<, == on int, str, list order) are given operations with role decide. A sealed sort has no order unless its interface declares one.

docs.title: 6.1 Kernel nodes
docs.text:
All bodies (of operations, combinators, observations, valid, canon) are trees of these nodes. Interpretation, tracing, type checking and cost accounting use the same tree.

node fields meaning Var name a parameter or a Let name Lit value a literal value (checked against the expected sort) Call fn, args call an operation, a definition, or an operation parameter; strict; names resolve to a local Rec function, then a scope definition or atom, then a variable holding an operation reference (an operation parameter must not share a name with a scope name) Let name, value, body evaluate value once, bind it Case arms: [(cond, body)], default ordered, short-circuit; first true arm wins Rec fn, params, body, measure a local recursive function (section 6.3) Blocks vars, entry, blocks a flat program with labelled blocks (section 6.4) Jump target / cond, then, else block terminator: goto, conditional goto Halt value block terminator: return

Conditions: Test(node) (the node evaluates to a bool card), And, Or, Not, True. Conditions evaluate left to right with short-circuit. If an evaluated condition is Bottom, the whole Case is Bottom(nan_condition). If no arm matches and there is no default, the result is Bottom(no_branch).

A world opens a subset of nodes in combinators.nodes. A body that uses a node the world does not open fails the type check.

docs.title: 6.2 Standard library combinators
docs.text:
A standard combinator is a CombinatorSpec with operation parameters and a public unfold rule written with kernel nodes:

name parameters unfold rule seq f, g x |-> g(f(x)) twice f x |-> f(f(x)) repeat f, n (static) n nested calls of f fold f, z Rec over a list: fold(f, z, nil) = z, fold(f, z, cons(h, t)) = f(h, fold(f, z, t)) map f Rec over a list repeat_until body, stop, max, on_exhaust section 13.2 for the legacy robot form search bound, p least i in 0..bound with p(i); Rec with measure bound - i

A world may declare more. A new combinator definition (kind combinator) has the same shape: parameters (values and operation parameters), a body, and its unfold rule is "substitute the passed operations and arguments into the body".

docs.title: 6.3 Rec
docs.text:
Rec(fn, params, body, measure) binds a recursive function fn. The body may call fn.

  • measure is a Node over params that returns a non-negative Int. At each recursive call the kernel evaluates the measure of the new arguments; it must be smaller than the measure of the current arguments, else the call is Bottom(measure). The measure is a termination check, not part of the computation: it is not charged and not traced, but it runs under the same fuel and depth limits as a separate budget; a measure that does not finish makes the call Unknown.
  • The recursion counter is updated by the world's own operations and charged like any call (clock %, bits shift_right, negative counters in legacy worlds). The kernel never inserts a hidden n - 1.
  • measure: fuel (allowed when the world sets combinators.recursion: fuel) means: no measure check; the recursion is bounded only by fuel and depth, and running out is Unknown. This is how a learner writes recursion without proving termination (the experiment worlds use it).
  • measure: legacy (dialect legacy-v1 only) means the same, with the legacy depth limit (10 000); exceeding it is Unknown(depth).
  • combinators.recursion of a world is one of legacy, measure (every Rec needs a measure node), fuel (a Rec may use measure: fuel), none (the world does not open Rec; a machine world repeats with Blocks/Jump). combinators.nodes may also list the block terminators Jump, CondJump, Halt next to Blocks.

docs.title: 6.4 Blocks and Jump
docs.text: Blocks(vars, entry, blocks) is a program with a program counter. Each block is a list of assignments var := node and one terminator (Jump, conditional Jump, Halt). Every executed jump charges one control step. Loops stop when the fuel runs out (Unknown(fuel)). A Blocks program is a combinator card. It is not a value and cannot modify itself (section 15).

docs.title: 6.5 Fuel and steps
docs.text:
• Layer-0 steps: each call of a given operation charges its declared cost (default 1); each executed Jump charges 1. Calls of definitions charge nothing themselves; their bodies charge.
  • Fuel is a budget in layer-0 steps. When it runs out the result is Unknown(fuel).
  • The step count and the fuel are always computed on the full unfolding to layer 0, whatever boundary is shown and whatever is promoted. A fast path for a promoted definition (section 9.7) must charge the exact layer-0 step count of the unfolding.
  • Legacy step count = the old base_ops count (calls of base operations).

docs.title: 7.1 World side
docs.text:
observation:
  truth: robot_state                # the sealed full state
  probes:                           # given read operations on the truth
    - {name: front_wall, sort: bool, reveals: ["whether the cell in front is a wall"]}
  capabilities:                     # per agent; default agent "learner"
    learner: {channels: [results, errors, renders, traces, steps, memory], probes: all}
  show: {input: full_state, result: full_state}   # what a task shows; may only narrow
  judge_view: full_state            # default; per task it may be a declared projection
  • The truth is sealed. Only probes read it.
  • channels lists what the learner sees: results, error reasons, renders, traces, step counts, memory (provisional default: all six).
  • Grading always uses judge_view applied to the full truth state, never the learner's view (invariant 3). Values: full_state (default), contract_projection(fields).

docs.title: 7.2 New observations (kind observation)
docs.text:
kind: observation
name: front_free
reads: [front_wall, front_water]     # granted probes only
memory: null                          # or {sort: int, init: <Lit>, step: <Node over memory and reads>}
body: "not front_wall and not front_water"   # a Node over the probe values and the memory

Rules checked by the type checker:

  • The body and memory.step may call only: probes in reads (each granted to the agent), other observation definitions, and operations whose inputs do not include the truth sort.
  • Memory is a fold over past observations: memory.step(previous_memory, current probe values). Memory never reads the truth directly.
  • An observation cannot change the truth: it has no act operation in its dependency closure.

Unfolding an observation shows the probes it reads ("front free" unfolds to two observations).

docs.title: 8. Definition record
docs.text:
id: "<world>@<version>/<name>"
name: MUL
kind: operation                       # object | operation | combinator | observation
origin: invented                      # given | invented
layer: 1                              # 0 for given; else at least 1 + max(layer of depends_on)
depends_on: [add, dec, jump]
spec: {...}                           # the ObjectSpec / OperationSpec / CombinatorSpec / ObservationSpec fields
body: <Node>                          # or {host: ...} for given atoms (HostRule)
evidence:
  method: exhaustive                  # exhaustive | bounded | sampled
  scope: {domain: "byte x byte", size: 65536, description: "all 8-bit pairs, full machine state"}
  seed: null                          # required for sampled
  checks: [unfold_equivalence, boundary_invariance]   # obligations covered
  world_hash: "<sha256>"
  deps_hash: "<sha256 of the transitive dependency records>"
contract:
  guarantees: "R0 = a * b mod 256"
  may_change: [R2, flags]             # descriptive; v1 promotion still needs full-state equality
  keeps: [memory]
cost:
  length: 14                          # nodes in the body
  steps: {min: 3, max: 1020, mean: 511.5, over: "verification scope"}   # exact layer-0 steps
  reuse: 0                            # call sites in other stored definitions and solutions
status: promoted                      # written | checked | callable | verified | promoted
  • layer of an invented definition is at least 1 + the highest layer of its dependencies (a definition may be placed higher, for example on a design row; never lower). Generated operations of an object have the object's layer; those of world objects are layer 0.
  • origin: given marks world atoms. origin: invented marks definitions written by a learner or a generator. Origin is never a performance shortcut.
  • Evidence is invalid when the world hash or a dependency changes. The library then resets the status to callable.
  • Evidence methods and their rights:
method meaning may be stored and called may be promoted exhaustive every input in the scope and every claimed answer checked yes yes, scope carried bounded every input up to a size bound yes yes, scope carried sampled seeded random inputs; seed and count recorded yes no

The library must never turn an exhaustive claim into a sampled one silently, and must never widen a scope.

docs.title: 9. The pipeline
docs.text:
1. written: the record has name, kind, body, depends_on. depends_on must equal the set of names the body references.
  2. checked: the type checker accepts the body: every name resolves in the world plus the library; sorts match; only opened nodes are used; observation and seal rules hold; valid/canon use the terminating sublanguage; no dependency cycle except inside a declared Rec or sort group.
  3. callable: the kernel runs the body and unfolds it to layer 0 on at least one input. Calls are charged by the unfolded layer-0 steps.
  4. verified: evidence is recorded (section 8) with the obligations of the kind:
kind obligations operation the result agrees with the reference (an oracle, a given operation it claims to equal, or a declared table) on the scope; unfold_equivalence object refine: canon total, idempotent, keeps validity; every interface operation respects canon; seal: no outside definition reads the inside. Invented vs given: an abstraction map abs that commutes with the interface, checked exhaustively in a recorded scope; else seeded random interface-program tests, labelled sampled combinator for every passed operation in a recorded finite family (the world's given operations and short compositions of them, listed in the scope) and every input in the scope, the combinator equals its unfold rule; always bounded or sampled observation dependency check (only granted probes and memory); the value agrees with the claimed reference on the scope (required for promotion); the truth is unchanged; two truth states with equal probe values give equal observations
  1. accounted: cost.length, cost.steps, cost.reuse are filled.
  2. stored: the library keeps the record and its dependency records. The definition can be called by name. It is not yet one step for display. A verification domain is never empty, and every input of it is checked (observations: every state of the domain; extra histories only order states for memory). Evidence also records the content hash of the definition and a digest of the layer-0 atom implementations; a change of either drops the evidence (also when a library is reloaded).
  3. promoted: allowed only when the method is exhaustive or bounded and the unfold-equivalence check passed on the scope on the full execution state (value, Bottom vs Ok, side effects on the state, layer-0 steps). The record keeps its scope and contract. Under a boundary that does not open it, a promoted definition is shown as one step.

docs.title: 9.7 Fast paths
docs.text: A promoted operation may carry a fast implementation used only inside its verified exhaustive scope. The fast path must return the same outcome and charge the exact layer-0 step count recorded for that input (or computed by an exact formula checked on the whole scope). Outside the scope the kernel runs the unfolding.

docs.title: 10. Boundaries
docs.text:
A boundary decides which calls of definitions are shown as one step and which are opened. It never changes the evaluation (invariant 2).

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Boundary:
    depth: int | None = None            # open definitions of layer >= depth (None: open none by depth)
    open_names: frozenset[str] = ...    # position: open these definitions wherever they occur
    keep_names: frozenset[str] = ...    # position: keep these as one step even if depth would open them
    open_paths: frozenset[tuple[int, ...]] = ...   # position: open the call at these call paths only
    kinds: frozenset[str] = ALL_KINDS   # kind: open only along these kinds (object|operation|combinator|observation)

A call of definition d at call path p is opened iff d is not given, d.kind is in kinds, d.name is not in keep_names, and one of: d.layer >= depth, d.name in open_names, p in open_paths. Given atoms are never opened.

  • The legacy cut(known, known_layers) is Boundary(depth=known_layers, keep_names=known) restricted to kind operation.
  • "Unfold everything" is Boundary(depth=0). "Unfold nothing" is Boundary().
  • Examples from the design: DOT kept; DOT opened with MUL kept (open_names={DOT}, keep_names={MUL}); everything to layer 0 (depth=0).
  • Kind examples: MUL opens into additions, three opens into succ calls, while opens into jumps, front_free opens into two probes.

Unfold-equivalence verifier (verify.unfold_equivalent in the package): for an expression, a list of boundaries and inputs, it evaluates under each boundary and checks equal outcome, equal final state, equal layer-0 step count, and that the flattened view of each boundary expands to the layer-0 trace.

docs.title: 11. The four invariants and their tests
docs.text: invariant rule test that must exist I1 always unfoldable every promoted definition unfolds to layer 0 and gives the same outcome for every stored definition: evaluation with Boundary() equals evaluation of the full unfolding, on the evidence scope I2 boundary never changes a result a boundary changes only step visibility random expressions x random boundaries: outcome, state and layer-0 steps identical; flattened views splice exactly I3 observation never changes facts grading uses judge_view(full truth) an observation definition run on a state leaves the state unchanged; grading with two learner views gives the same verdict I4 promotion carries scope and contract evidence and contract travel with the promoted record promoting without evidence, with sampled, or with a changed world hash fails; a derived world lists the scope of each promoted definition

docs.title: 12. World declaration (schema opulse.world/2)
docs.text:
world: clock
version: 2
dialect: atoms-v2                     # or legacy-v1
params: {}
constants: {}
objects: [hour]                       # ObjectSpec records (given, layer 0)
operations: [add, sub, mul, div, mod, neg, reverse, triangle, popcount, digitsum]
combinators: {nodes: [Var, Lit, Call, Let, Case, Rec], library: [], recursion: legacy}
observation: {truth: null, show: {input: values, result: value}, judge_view: full_state}
lock: {host_digests: {...}, constants_hash: "...", world_hash: "..."}

Extra members. A world, an object, an operation and a probe may carry extra members (world title, title_zh, source, codec; operation symbol, input_names; object host, doc; probe impl; others allowed). Readers keep them in an extra dict and write them back unchanged. The world hash excludes the display-only members title, title_zh, doc, source, symbol, input_names, and includes every other member.

Derived world: {"extends": "<world>@<version>", "promoted": ["<definition id>", ...]}. A derived world adds promoted definitions as layer-k atoms with their scope and contract. World B + promoted MUL gives the same results as world A with given MUL; step counts and learning may differ (B charges the unfolded steps).

docs.title: 13.1 Mapping of the current code
docs.text: current atoms-v2 core/types.py ValueType (int, bool, str, list[int], perm[n], grid, note, melody, state, colour, direction) given ObjectSpecs of the world, with host codecs Operator with definition is None (base atoms, CUSTOM primitives) Definition(kind=operation, origin=given, layer=0, body=HostRule) generated Operator with a definition Definition(kind=operation, origin=invented, layer=recursive_layer) definition_type SIMPLE / BRANCH / RECURSIVE body without Case / with Case / with a self call in Case (Rec, measure: legacy). The old definition_type is kept as metadata, never re-derived Search node search combinator: bounded Rec + ordered Case; legacy steps count only the atoms inside the predicate; definition_type stays SIMPLE Compare in conditions a call of a given decide operation (int.lt, ...) with legacy order NAN Bottom; same_value(NAN, NAN) stays true OperatorRegistry the definition library of a world trace/tree.cut(known, known_layers) Boundary(depth=known_layers, keep_names=known) interpreter Result(value, base_ops, calls) Outcome, layer-0 steps = base_ops robot Skill (repeat / guard) repeat_until and Case over probes, dialect form Semantics.mode exact / legacy / modular output edge enter: bottom on overflow / fold(legacy_bound) / normalize(mod m)

docs.title: 13.2 Dialect rules (all required for golden equality)
docs.text:
1. Robot repeat_until(body, stop, max): max = 0 returns the state; each round checks stop first, then runs body; after max rounds it returns the last state without checking stop again. An illegal forward is Bottom(blocked), never "stay in place".
  2. Pitch: where a note parameter receives an int, the dialect inserts a counted make_note check 0..127; out of range is Bottom(invalid). note -> int is implicit.
  3. Legacy integer mode: results fold symmetrically by the bound; reverse, triangle, digitsum preprocess the input with abs(a) % bound; division and modulo by zero use divisor 1. These are input-edge and output-edge rules of the dialect (fold(legacy)).
  4. Legacy recursion: counters are updated by the world operations (clock %, bits shift_right, negative counters). No measure check; depth limit 10 000.
  5. search keeps its old node, old steps and old traces.
  6. Old tags: perm gets its n from the world; packed integer aliases (swap, recolour) are expanded by the codec; nan maps to Bottom; the empty grid crop ((0,),) stays.
  7. Conditions: short-circuit and/or; a NaN condition aborts the definition (legacy reason nan_condition).
  8. NaN flows as a value: every argument of a call is evaluated even when an earlier one is Bottom; a given atom with Bottom arguments is still called and charged (legacy host functions return NaN, defined returns 0); a definition with Bottom arguments is entered with its parameters bound to Bottom; Let binds Bottom. Only Unknown stops evaluation. Comparisons are given decide atoms of cost 0 (legacy step counts include only base operations).

docs.title: 13.3 Codec and golden tests
docs.text: The codec of a world maps legacy tag -> sort with the world context (for example perm -> perm[n], clock int -> hour). Golden tests read every published example in docs/assets/data/worlds/<w>.json (and seed files, steps files, tasks) and must reproduce the outputs, failures, step counts and traces through the new kernel in dialect legacy-v1. The only exception is the clock world (section 14), whose data is regenerated.

docs.title: 14. Clock world: a true clock (world clock, version 2)
docs.text:
• Object hour = refine int; canon n |-> n mod 12 (values 0..11). Entry rule normalize on every operation input, every literal and every task input: 14 enters as 2, -4 enters as 8.
  • Every operation takes canonical hours and returns an hour (out.enter: normalize). reverse, digitsum, triangle, popcount act on the 0..11 representation, so they are well defined on hours. Division and modulo by 0 are Bottom(div_zero).
  • Recursion counters use the clock operations (as before).
  • The clock data in docs/assets/data/worlds/clock* and the site examples are regenerated. Old golden examples whose inputs are outside 0..11 are not compared. This is the only intended change to published answers.

docs.title: 15. Computer world v1 (Harvard style)
docs.text:
• Objects: byte = refine int where 0 <= x < 256; reg = compose <r0 | r1 | r2 | r3>; flag = bool; machine_state = compose <machine(regs: array[4, byte], mem: array[256, byte], zero: flag, carry: flag)> (registers are fields of the machine state).
  • Operations: read(state, reg) -> byte, write(state, reg, byte) -> state, load, store, add (wraps, sets carry), dec, is_zero. Each with rule, errors, cost 1.
  • Combinators: Blocks/Jump with conditional jump; sequence. The program is a separate combinator card, not in memory, and cannot modify itself.
  • Observation: inputs and output, or all registers; per task.
  • First experiment target: MUL as an invented operation (loop of add and dec), verified exhaustively on 65 536 input pairs with the full machine state; contract states which registers it changes.

docs.title: 16. Not in v1 (documented limits)
docs.text:
• (Moved into scope 11-04: definitions as objects, meta worlds, world building and self-modifying code are built by the meta level; see the atoms-meta spec on the meta branch.)
  • Infinite objects: streams, codata, corecursion.
  • Narrow (contract-only) promotion: v1 promotion requires full-state equality.
  • Proof certificates as evidence method; tolerance / prefix / three-valued answers.

docs.title: 18.1 Open kinds
docs.text: A world declares open_kinds, a subset of the six kinds (default: the four layer-0 kinds, so older declarations keep their hash; JSON: a sorted list; part of the world hash). The library refuses to store an invented definition whose kind is closed. Old Opulse is open_kinds = [operation] (legacy_world_decl).

docs.title: 18.2 More combination modes
docs.text:
Each has a public unfold to kernel nodes and exact layer-0 cost; each passes through the library pipeline with bounded or sampled evidence over a declared operation family.

mode form unfold fixpoint until stable @fix[step] (x, height) Rec with measure = remaining height; equal consecutive values stop; exhausting the declared finite height is Bottom(not_stable) memoized recursion Rec(..., memo=True) same outcome and the same charged steps as the plain recursion; the kernel reports the memo work separately (Run.work) turns @turns[observe_i, choose_i, apply] (state, schedule) each agent chooses from its own observation only; schedules: round-robin with a count, an explicit order, or all orders up to a bound (the list of distinct final states) derived structural recursion @S.fold[on_tag...] (value), S.size(value) every compose object (and sort group) gets its fold (one case per tag, recursive fields folded first; measure S.size) and its size (constructor count, cost 1)

A combinator body may pass its own operation parameter on to another combinator; this records a dependency edge. Literals may hold an operation reference ({"t": "fn", "v": name}) and a declared failure ({"t": "bottom", "v": reason}).

docs.title: 18.3 Generic probes
docs.text:
Probes are the atoms of kind observation named in observation.probes; they take the truth value. An observation may call probes and other observations; it may not call an operation whose role is act or whose inputs include the truth sort. The observed value is the observation's subject (ObservationSpec.extra["subject"], default s). ?p{s} is Call(p, (Var(s),)); the subject may be passed only to probes and observations.

Since 0.5 (decision R13-D): a derived observation may apply pure definitions (operations, combinators, bridges, other observations) to observed values, provided nothing in its dependency closure has role act or takes the truth sort, and the truth subject still reaches only probes and observations. An observation may also observe public values: extra["inputs"] lists several typed inputs, none of the truth sort; it is then a pure function of those inputs, facts_unchanged applies to the inputs and non_interference does not apply (recorded as n/a).

docs.title: 18.4 Content identity
docs.text: Definition.content_hash(deps) hashes the kind, the spec without display-only members, the body and the content hashes of the dependencies. Parameter names are semantic (they bind the body). Evidence records the content hash; promotion refuses a definition whose content hash changed. A promoted definition is immutable: a change is a new definition (force_new_version) that inherits no evidence.

docs.title: 18.5 ASCII notation
docs.text: The only written form of definitions, prompts and data is ASCII (atoms.notation: printer and parser, exact inverses). Four kinds, four brackets: objects Frac<1, 2>, List<1, 2>; operations mul(3, 4); combinators @twice[double] (3); observations ?even{12}. Comparisons are operations (lt, le, eq, ne); only given + - * may be infix. Declarations start with obj, op, comb, obs and end with given or L<n>. The sigils @ and ? are notation only: stored names are plain identifiers. Generated names: objects A0..Z0, A1..; operations f6; combinators @k3; observations ?q4; old Unicode operator symbols map to f<n> through the legacy codec.

docs.title: 18.6 Metered atoms
docs.text: Atom(metered=True) receives a context whose call(defn, args, extra_defns, budget) evaluates inside the running evaluation: the same step counter, fuel, depth and trace (inner calls are children of the atom's frame). The atom itself costs 0; a budget overrun is Unknown(fuel) for the atom. This is how eval(code, args) keeps exact layer-0 steps (meta level).

docs.title: 19.1 Laws (kind law, sigil #)
docs.text: LawSpec(name, vars, statement): statement is a boolean node over the typed vars. ASCII: law #mul_comm: eq(mul(a, b), mul(b, a)) for a: Int, b: Int L1 (given for axioms). Evidence is the usual: every tuple of the domain makes the statement Ok(true); the scope is recorded and never widened (a law checked on 8-bit values is not a law for all widths). An equation eq(lhs, rhs) may serve as ONE rewrite step by #law in a derivation once promoted. The step matches one side against a subterm (law variables bind subterms) and substitutes the other side. The derivation must still unfold to layer 0 with the same result: the rewrite is replayed as computation, and every binding of the law's variables must lie inside the verified scope; outside the scope the step is refused. A rewrite step costs no layer-0 step; the charged steps are those of evaluating the final expression.

docs.title: 19.2 Bridges (kind bridge, sigil ~)
docs.text: BridgeSpec(name, source, target, map, domain, interface): map is a node over x, domain an optional boolean node over x (partial bridges: outside it the bridge is Bottom(outside_domain)), interface pairs (source operation, target operation). ASCII: bridge ~to_frac: MyFrac -> Frac, applied as ~to_frac(x). Obligation (commutes): on the recorded scope, translate-then-compute equals compute-then-translate for every interface pair. Cross-world bridges name world@version:sort. The invented-vs-given abstraction check (section 8) and the meta compiler are bridges. A composed bridge has its own evidence.

docs.title: 19.3 Templates
docs.text: TemplateSpec(name, params, produces, pattern): parameters are (name, kind or sort); the pattern is the produced spec with $param placeholders. Example: obj Quot[T, canon] = refine T canon(canon); Frac = Quot[Pair<Int, Int>, reduce], Hour = Quot[Int, mod12]. A template is checked once as a family (bounded or sampled evidence over a recorded finite family of instantiations, never exhaustive). Every instantiation is an ordinary definition with its own pipeline and evidence; it may cite the template's evidence only for arguments inside the recorded family. Content identity covers template and arguments; instantiations list the template in depends_on, so a boundary can open Frac into Quot[...] and then into its body.

docs.title: 17. Reference implementation (Python) and versions
docs.text:
Package opulse.atoms (new; the old code keeps working unchanged):

module contents atoms.values Card, Ok, Bottom, Unknown, outcome_equal, value_equal, JSON codec opulse.value/2 atoms.nodes kernel nodes (section 6.1), conditions, JSON round trip, length() atoms.kernel evaluate(node, env, world, library, fuel) -> (Outcome, Steps, Trace); strictness, Case, Rec, Blocks atoms.spec ObjectSpec, OperationSpec, CombinatorSpec, ObservationSpec, Definition, Evidence, Contract, Cost, Status atoms.world WorldDecl, derived worlds, world hash atoms.boundary Boundary, opens(), legacy from_cut() atoms.verify unfold_equivalent, evidence builders (exhaustive / bounded / sampled), object, combinator and observation obligations atoms.library Library: add, check, run, verify, account, store, promote; invalidation atoms.legacy dialect legacy-v1: registry and robot skills -> kernel scope; legacy definition records atoms.golden golden harness: every published example through the current engine or the kernel engine atoms.check the type checker of pipeline step 2 atoms.objects object operations (constructors, accessors, make, seal) and object obligations atoms.observations robot probes, observation runs over histories, non-interference, judge atoms.combinators the standard combinators, instantiate, combinator obligations over an operation family atoms.notation the ASCII notation: printer, parser, generated names (section 18.5) atoms.random_programs seeded random kernel programs and hypothesis strategies for the invariant tests

JSON schemas: values opulse.value/2; definitions opulse.definition/2; worlds opulse.world/2. Each JSON object written by the reference implementation carries its schema field.

docs.text:

docs.title: Research uses
docs.text: RESEARCH / 01   USE CASES

docs.title: Finite traces need external tests
docs.text:
A finite world fixes its operations, permitted observations, and judge view. Opulse records definitions, outcomes, and layer-0 costs under that contract. A trace shows what happened inside that world; it does not show that a model improves on external tasks. The versions design below asks what a merge trace could be used to measure, not what it already proves.

Designed example (versions design record)

The versions@1 design record specifies two paths, three possible texts, an immutable parent ledger and a conflict value. Its stored outcome is a historical export, not a model or policy evaluation.

docs.title: One artifact, three questions
docs.text:
01 / FINITE RL

02 / PROCESS LABELS

03 / DIAGNOSTIC PAIRS

docs.title: Can an agent learn to resolve a conflict?
docs.text:
Designed example (versions design record)

State: a base version, two edited descendants, and the visible conflict record. Action: choose a permitted merge or resolution operation. Reward: a task-specific score for the resulting version, computed by a full-state judge. State and action are typed; a high task reward alone does not certify that a definition unfolds equivalently.

Compare a policy using only granted probes with one that sees the entire parent ledger. That comparison is a leakage audit, not a fair baseline for the restricted policy.

docs.title: Where did a derivation fail?
docs.text:
Designed example (versions design record)

Each attempted step needs an outcome, a scope and a reason. A process reward model scores individual steps. Candidate labels are Ok(value), Bottom(reason) and Unknown(resource); no model was trained on this export. A merge conflict can be an Ok value; do not recast it as Bottom. Unknown(fuel) means evaluation ran out of budget and never counts as correct.

docs.title: Same answer, different path?
docs.text:
Designed example (versions design record)

Pair runs that end in the same projected task answer but differ in provenance, conflict handling, trace, or exact layer-0 cost. Keep both complete records. A model that predicts the same final answer for both may still make different process errors; inspect the divergence before treating either run as valid.

docs.title: Trace to use
docs.text:
Designed example (versions design record)

The historical export records an apply operation that changes two independent document paths in one state change, with 119 layer-0 steps and an Ok outcome. Its displayed call is not runnable parser source, so it is not reproduced here. A study of conflict handling would need competing edits and an external test.

World + scopeversion, probes, judge view Typed traceoutcome, cost, full state Research questionpolicy / PRM / paired records External test missingreal tasks, people, transfer

docs.title: What is not established
docs.text:
The legacy operation-only experiments motivate these designs, but their metrics are not atoms-v2 results. A study still needs independent ground truth, pinned splits, matched baselines, uncertainty across seeds, and held-out environments. No current artifact here measures improvement in human decision-making, general model reasoning, or transfer to real version-control systems. Write a protocol before claiming any of those outcomes.

docs.title: Research experiments
docs.text: RESEARCH / 03   EXPERIMENTS

docs.title: Change the boundary. Keep the computation.
docs.text:
The grammar design separates strings from their derivation trees. A split operation can feed a reusable parser combinator. The old parse-count sketch reads a parse-count probe; spec 0.5 also permits an observation to apply a pure combinator to observed values. It cannot act or read the truth except through probes. The grammar tower is still a design until rebuilt and checked on the 0.5 core. A promotion study could compare one checked parser shown open versus closed. This page specifies a test, not a result.

Designed example (grammar design record)

The grammar@1 historical export stores 58,669 layer-0 steps for the parse-count observation on eight operands separated by plus signs, with a successful outcome. That historical export uses machine notation, not a v3 display formula. Recompute costs from the kernel for every study input before reporting results; no ablation was run.

docs.title: Promotion ablation / pre-register
docs.text:
CONTROL / OPEN BOUNDARY

Designed example (grammar design record)

Give the agent the same typed grammar, examples and tasks. Expand the parser at the chosen call boundary so each internal call is visible. Charge the exact layer-0 cost for the full unfolding. Supply the same context budget, tools, training records and test split as the promoted condition.

Visible trace length changes; full-state output and charged layer-0 steps must not.

TREATMENT / CLOSED BOUNDARY

Designed example (grammar design record)

Give the same agent a checked, promoted parser as one visible callable step with its hash, contract, and evidence scope attached. Do not use the promotion outside the checked scope. Unfold it for auditing and charge exactly the same layer-0 cost as in control.

A shorter displayed derivation is not a faster kernel evaluation.

Primary outcome: success on held-out, exactly scoped parse/count questions. Secondary outcomes: first wrong trace step, Bottom and Unknown rates, visible context tokens, and layer-0 cost per solved item. Compare plain and memoized recursion only when both versions record their exact layer-0 costs and identical outcomes. Seed and publish every split, model checkpoint, prompt, definition hash, boundary, and checker version.

docs.title: Study 01 / Parser promotion
docs.text:
Designed example (grammar design record)

  • Hypothesis: a scoped promoted parser improves held-out parse/count success over the same parser shown unfolded.
  • Control: the same grammar, inputs, agent, tools, and budget with an open boundary; compare exact layer-0 costs.
  • Failure criterion: no matched-control gain, mismatched outcome or cost, scope violations, or a gain lost on held-out structures.
  • Limitation: a shorter visible trace does not mean faster execution or transfer to new grammars.
  • Available today: grammar@1 design record. No parser promotion study or model checkpoint.

docs.title: Five more proposed studies
docs.text:
The proposed to-frac bridge below has no implemented translation or checked commuting contract. The core can execute and verify bridges: Learn / Checks shows a bounded to-difference check from the kernel walkthrough. A transfer study still needs a versioned, scoped to-frac instance and trial.

These designs adapt ideas from the former operations-only experiment, environment, interpretation, and compilation guides. Those earlier Legacy-v1 protocols and any old model scores do not constitute atoms-v2 measurements. Specify visibility and split controls before collecting data.

The archived Legacy-v1 model-internals experiment uses the optional interp extra. Its dependency marker is not an atoms-v2 study or a command to run one:

# requires: opulse[interp]

NEXT / Build a world Browse world designs Review protocol controls

docs.title: Study 02 / Concept invention
docs.text:
Designed example (grammar design record)

  • Hypothesis: checked novel definitions help on later tasks beyond a fixed library.
  • Control: given-library-only and renamed-definition baselines on identical tasks.
  • Failure criterion: no gain in valid novel definitions and held-out task reward.
  • Limitation: a new name alone is not a new concept.
  • Available today: grammar@1 design record; no invention trial or reward measurements.

docs.title: Study 03 / Mechanistic interpretation
docs.text:
Designed example (grammar design record)

  • Hypothesis: model states encode a trace's intermediate typed values.
  • Control: shuffled-label probe, with definition hashes held out.
  • Failure criterion: no out-of-split advantage over shuffled labels or no intervention effect.
  • Limitation: decoding a value does not establish causal use.
  • Available today: grammar@1 design record; no model states or probe results.

docs.title: Study 04 / Autoformalization
docs.text:
Designed example (action design record)

  • Hypothesis: a model can produce typed definitions and auditable outcome contracts from task text.
  • Control: hand-authored specifications checked by the same independent checker.
  • Failure criterion: invalid types, mismatched outcomes, or no improvement over control.
  • Limitation: success on finite cases does not imply universal correctness.
  • Available today: action@2 design record; no paired formalization results.

docs.title: Study 05 / Model-side compilation
docs.text:
Designed example (grammar design record)

  • Hypothesis: a compact intermediate representation improves deeper compositional tasks.
  • Control: direct prompting, shuffled slot map, and unfolded representation.
  • Failure criterion: no advantage on held-out depth with equal context and tools.
  • Limitation: an execution smoke test does not establish model learning.
  • Available today: grammar@1 design record; no compilation trial.

docs.title: Study 06 / Cross-world transfer
docs.text:
Designed example (grammar design record)

  • Hypothesis: a checked bridge preserves answers on held-out tasks across worlds.
  • Control: matched within-world policy and an unbridged cross-world policy.
  • Failure criterion: commuting check fails within scope or no held-out advantage.
  • Limitation: one bounded bridge does not prove general transfer.
  • Available today: grammar@1 design record and a bounded, executable bridge example for to-difference; to-frac remains an unimplemented design, with no transfer trial.

docs.title: Research protocols
docs.text: RESEARCH / 02   PROTOCOLS

docs.title: Audit what an agent can actually see
docs.text:
The published action@2 design record describes a 12x10 grid and separate front-wall and front-water probes. A proposed learner policy uses only the probes and actions authorized by that contract; a full-map oracle is a separate baseline. The judge grades against full state.

Download the action audit protocol template to start from a versioned JSON manifest. It pins the design record and its file digest; run-only fields are empty. Complete those fields before a run.

docs.title: Download the pinned source bundle
docs.text:
Designed example (source design bundle; no run)

The bundle includes a seeded split of older action@1 task IDs. It has no action@2 maze episodes or evaluation results.

Download the complete source bundle (ZIP) or open its manifest. Its files are also available individually: world export, declaration, stored lock, task IDs, seeded split, and metric definition. All six files have SHA-256 digests in the manifest. Rebuild with python tools/research_bundle.py from a checkout; the script also supports a staleness-check mode.

Read the linked manifest for the file digests and unavailable fields.

The family-disjoint split covers existing task IDs, not environment layouts. The manifest lists missing episode, checker and run artifacts. The metric is a definition, not a measured score.

Designed example (action audit template)

Audit question: on the same bounded maze and action budget, does a probe-only policy avoid unsafe moves as often as a full-map oracle? The oracle has information the learner does not. Report both separately; do not train or tune the learner on hidden maps from its test split.

docs.title: Observation boundary
docs.text:
LEARNER / AUTHORIZED

  • Own action and observation history.
  • Front-wall and front-water probe outputs, when granted.
  • Only the result, error, render, trace, step-count, and memory channels explicitly declared in the protocol.

The observation function reads authorized probes and past observations. It must not inspect the hidden map or silently use the judge view. Restrict interactive tools and serialized features too.

JUDGE / HELD BACK

  • Sealed full state, including positions and obstacles.
  • Exact Ok(value), Bottom(reason), and Unknown(resource) outcomes.
  • Layer-0 cost charged through promoted definitions; the visible boundary cannot change a result or its charged cost.

The judge computes task reward from its declared view. It also checks full-state equivalence before promotion; matching projected reward is insufficient.

docs.title: Freeze this record before a run
docs.text:
Field Minimum declaration Why it matters World and checker World name, declaration version/hash, kernel version, checker version, schema version Prevents a changed rule from inheriting old evidence. Units State-generation seed, environment split, episode IDs, maximum turns, layer-0 fuel Makes an Unknown(fuel) reproducible. Visibility Agent identity, permitted probes, operations, all visible channels, judge view Detects a hidden-state shortcut. Definition Source/hash, dependencies, kind, layer, contract and check scope Binds promotion to the version actually checked. Evaluation Answer shape, scope, baseline policy, reward function, failure criterion Separates one witness from all solutions. Artifact Input manifest, trace/output hashes, evaluator log and source revision Makes later audits possible.

Split rule: split by environment layout and initial state before generating trajectories. Keep validation and test seeds disjoint from training; report how duplicates or isomorphic maps are removed. A public world declaration is not a secret test answer. Baseline rule: report a random legal-action policy, a probe-only hand-specified policy, and a full-map oracle in separate columns. Do not describe the oracle as a fair restricted policy.

docs.title: Leakage checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Results and Bottom reasons do not name hidden cells.
  • [ ] Renders and trace nodes hide judge-only state and private arguments.
  • [ ] Step counts, fuel exhaustion, and latency cannot encode forbidden map features.
  • [ ] Memory, caches, tool responses, feedback, and retry histories obey the same visibility policy.
  • [ ] Saved prompts, example solutions, train/test generators, and version files cannot reveal held-out answers.
  • [ ] An unauthorized-probe request fails; the judge still sees full state for grading.

docs.title: Report without overclaiming
docs.text:
Give the exact domain and method. Use Exhaustively checked (scope ...) only for a completed enumeration with an artifact. Use Bounded (scope ...) only for a recorded bound. A Seeded sample never licenses promotion. Publish Ok, Bottom, and Unknown counts separately, with layer-0 step distributions and each policy's per-split reward. Confidence intervals across seeds describe variability, not mathematical equivalence. The older benchmark and corpus methods apply only to the Legacy-v1 operator dialect unless rerun with a pinned atoms-v2 world, checker, and visibility contract.
